Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Each line's characters drawn together**: where krkr_richtext draws the message window, a line's characters are shaped and drawn together by its `StyledLayout`, as its line breaker lays them out: kerning and ligatures run across the line, and accents and emoji made of several characters come out as one (a combining accent was drawn beside its letter, and an emoji as two boxes). KAG still places and times every character, so the text speed, waits, links and ruby are as before (`useStyledLayout` in `Config.tjs`)
- **Japanese and Chinese line breaks by krkr_richtext**: closing brackets, full stops, commas and small kana don't start a line, and a word in Latin letters isn't split across lines, as KAG's character wrap split it. Vertical text, and the web and iOS builds (no krkr_richtext), keep KAG's own wrap
- kagex-release 0.12.1 downloads the 0.12.1 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.12.1/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
